newsitem.title: UK: LME copper slips back on warehouse stock concerns.
newsitem.headline: LME copper slips back on warehouse stock concerns.

text.p: Copper prices gave back all the day's gains in late trading to end lower as the market reacted to rumours that London Metal Exchange stock figyres would be either side of unchanged on Friday.
"Averaging that out could mean a small up and there was also some determined spec selling on Comex this afternoon," one traders aid.
The expectation in the market earlier in the day had been for a decline of some 5,000/10,000 tonnes.
At 1800 GMT three months copper was indicated at $1,930/$1,935. It closed the kerb with an eight-dollar gain at $1,958 after briefly crossing the the key $1,970 resistance.
"It tried to tip up and it failed, basically," said a trader.
Aluminium came under pressure from producer selling earlier in the day and that helped to loosen copper's grip on the upside too, the trader said.
Three months aluminium was quoted at $1,429/$1,431 about $6.00 below the kerb close and showing a gain of only around three dollars from Wednesday.
The other metals were also easier following copper and aluminmium in the evening session.
